title: Can you provide QuickBooks API access for historical client data to build our internal dashboard, including any API limits, restrictions, and charges? | QuickBooks Community
snippet:
Yes, you can pull historical accounting and transaction data into your dashboard through the QuickBooks Online Accounting API, and setting up developer access itself is free. Here's how each piece works.
### Getting API access
1. Create a free account at the [Intuit Developer Portal](https://developer.intuit.com/app/developer/qbo/docs/get-started/start-developing-your-app), separate from your regular QuickBooks Online login.
2. From your developer dashboard, create an app and select QuickBooks Online. This generates your client ID and client secret, plus a free sandbox company for testing.
3. Each of your clients' QuickBooks Online companies will need to individually connect and authorize your app through OAuth 2.0, since access is scoped per company (per "realm ID"). There's no single connection that pulls data across all your managed clients at once, so each client authorizes the connection to their own books.

API access itself runs on a separate track from your QuickBooks Online subscription, through Intuit's App Partner Program. As of this program's rollout, API calls are split into two types:
- **Core calls** (mostly creating or updating records) are free and unmetered on every tier.
- **CorePlus calls** (mostly reading data and pulling reports, which is what your dashboard would rely on) are metered. The free Builder tier includes 500,000 CorePlus calls per month at no cost. Beyond that, paid tiers (Silver, Gold, Platinum) add higher monthly credit allotments with per-call overage pricing.
For a reporting dashboard like yours, you'd likely start on the free Builder tier and only need to consider a paid tier if your combined client data volume pushes past that monthly CorePlus allowance.
Full tier and pricing details can be found here: [Intuit App Partner Program Guide](https://static.developer.intuit.com/resources/Intuit_App_Partner_Program_Guide.pdf)

title: apideck.com/blog/quickbooks-api-pricing-and-the-intuit-app-partner-program
snippet:
Intuit introduced a significant change in 2025 with the launch of the [Intuit App Partner Program](https://blogs.intuit.com/2025/05/15/introducing-the-intuit-app-partner-program/). This new program introduces a tiered pricing model that distinguishes between different types of API operations, offering free unlimited access for data creation and updates while implementing usage-based pricing for data retrieval operations. Whether you're building a simple invoice sync or a comprehensive financial dashboard, the pricing tier you choose will depend on how much data your application needs to read from QuickBooks versus how much data it pushes into the system.
## QuickBooks Online vs QuickBooks Desktop
**Important Note**: The Intuit App Partner Program and its associated pricing structure **only applies to QuickBooks Online (QBO)** integrations. If you're building integrations with the [QuickBooks Desktop API](https://www.apideck.com/blog/build-an-integration-with-quickbooks-desktop-in-2025), this pricing model does not apply to you.
This pricing information is specifically for:
- ✅ **QuickBooks Online API** (REST API)
- ❌ **QuickBooks Desktop/Enterprise**

### Core API Calls (Free & Unlimited)
- **What they include**: Most data-in operations such as creating or updating records
- **Examples**: POST requests to create/update invoices, bills, customers, vendors, accounts, payments, etc.
- **Pricing**: Completely free and unlimited across all partner tiers
- **HTTP Methods**: Primarily POST operations for pushing data into QuickBooks
### CorePlus API Calls (Metered & Charged)
- **What they include**: Most data-out operations such as reading and querying data
- **Examples**: GET requests to retrieve accounts, query company information, fetch reports, read invoices, etc.
- **Pricing**: Free up to certain monthly limits, then charged based on usage
- **HTTP Methods**: Primarily GET operations for downloading data from QuickBooks
## Partner Tiers and Pricing Structure
The new program includes four partner tiers with different pricing models:
![QuickBooks API pricing](//images.ctfassets.net/d6o5ai4eeewt/5eevWdLgBlQSRMYEYg9SeM/2a81456f9f006dbab42dec1b199f66b2/Screenshot_2025-09-20_at_14.16.11.png)
### Builder Tier (Free)
- **Monthly Fee**: $0
- **Core API Calls**: Unlimited (free)
- **CorePlus API Credits**: 500,000 per month
- **Overage**: API calls are **blocked** after exceeding the 500,000 limit
- **Premium API Access**: Not included
- **Best For**: Small developers

title: QuickBooks API Integration (2026): Options, Pricing, Walkthrough
snippet:
| Interface | QuickBooks | Format | Direction | Best for |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **Online Accounting API** | Online | REST, JSON, OAuth 2.0 | read and write, near real time | any web application, assistants, ongoing sync |
| **SDK and Web Connector** | Desktop | SOAP and qbXML | read and write, on a schedule | connecting Desktop to web software |
| **File import** | Online: CSV, Excel. Desktop: IIF | text files | mostly in | one-off loads, migrations |
| **ODBC driver** | Desktop and Online (third party, such as QODBC) | SQL | mostly read | reporting in Excel, Power BI, SQL tools |
### Online Accounting API
A hosted REST API. You register an app on Intuit's developer portal, the user approves access once on Intuit's consent page, and your software calls `https://quickbooks.api.intuit.com/v3/company/{realmId}/...` with a bearer token. It has a SQL-like query language, full create, read, update and delete on customers, items, invoices, bills, payments and the rest, and reports. This is the one to build on if you run QuickBooks Online.

Since Intuit's App Partner Program started charging on 1 November 2025, API calls come in two kinds. **Core** calls put data in (creating or updating records) and are free and unlimited on every tier. **CorePlus** calls take data out (queries, reads, reports) and are metered.
| Tier | Monthly fee | CorePlus reads included | Above that |
|---|---|---|---|
| Builder | $0 | 500,000 a month | Blocked until next month |
| Silver | $300 | 1 million | $3.50 per 1,000 up to 10 million |
| Gold | $1,700 | 10 million | $1.40 per 1,000 up to 75 million |
| Platinum | $4,500 | 75 million | $0.25 per 1,000 |

Register an app on developer.intuit.com with the `com.intuit.quickbooks.accounting` scope, then send the user to Intuit's consent page:
```
https://appcenter.intuit.com/connect/oauth2
?client_id=...&response_type=code
&scope=com.intuit.quickbooks.accounting
&redirect_uri=http://localhost:8765/callback
&state=<random>
```

title: QuickBooks API: Setup, Pricing and Errors (2026 Guide)
snippet:
The QuickBooks API is [Intuit](https://www.intuit.com/oidam/intuit/ic/en_us/content/intuit-fact-sheet-document-icom-20240401.pdf)'s REST interface for reading and writing a QuickBooks Online company's accounting data, and it is the same interface that no-code tools such as [Activepieces](https://www.activepieces.com) call behind the scenes.
Access needs a free Intuit developer account and an app, and each customer's company authorizes that app. Checked 19 Nov 2026 against [Intuit's developer docs](https://developer.intuit.com).

Whichever plan you select, API access is available: the main API targets QuickBooks Online, and an app can connect to all three plans below, so plan selection can prioritize factors other than API access.

| Plan | Price per month | Users included | API access (checked 19 Nov 2026) |
|---|---|---|---|
| Simple Start | $38 | 1 | App can connect |
| Essentials | $85 | 3 | App can connect |
| Plus | $140 | 5 | App can connect |

Create the developer account, then an app with the accounting scope, and Intuit issues a client ID and client secret per environment, sandbox and production. Treat the secret as a credential with a named owner.

Intuit meters API calls by tier, and the cost doesn't scale in a straight line. [Tierguard](https://tierguard.dev/guides/quickbooks-api-cost) puts the Silver-tier bill at $300 a month for 1M calls, which is a modest line item.

At 5M calls it reaches $14,300 a month, so a fivefold increase in volume multiplies the bill nearly 48 times. At 10M calls it's $31,800 a month, so doubling again more than doubles the cost.

The free plan includes unlimited flows and 1,000 credits a month, so you can set the connection up and try it without paying anything.

**Is the QuickBooks API free to use?**
Creating an Intuit developer account and a sandbox company hasn't required payment. Intuit has changed how it prices API access, so confirm the current terms on Intuit's developer pricing page before you build.
Then ask who pays: the connection belongs to a specific QuickBooks company, and the cost should sit with whoever owns it.

**Where do I check current QuickBooks API changes?**
Start with Intuit's developer documentation, specifically its release notes and its pages on rate limits and error codes. Check them before each production release, not only when something fails.
Limits, token rules and endpoint versions are Intuit's to change, and any figure in a blog post, this one included, can be out of date.

title: truto.one/blog/how-much-does-the-quickbooks-api-cost-2026-pricing-rate-limits
snippet:
<cite index="5-3,5-4">On May 15, 2025, Intuit announced the App Partner Program, which introduces platform service fees for developers based on a tiered model. It went live on July 28, 2025, marking a departure from Intuit's traditionally open-access approach to its developer ecosystem.</cite> Writing data to QuickBooks remains free, but reading data is now strictly metered. The free Builder tier gives you 500,000 read operations per month before blocking further requests. Paid tiers range from **$300/month to $4,500/month**, with overage fees on top. Combined with strict rate limits (500 requests/minute, 10 concurrent), a 1-hour access token expiry, and the engineering effort to handle it all, the real cost of a QuickBooks integration goes well beyond what's on Intuit's pricing page.

<cite index="5-5">For decades, Intuit provided free or low-cost access to its development tools, APIs, and app marketplaces, encouraging third-party innovation.</cite> B2B SaaS companies treated the QuickBooks API as a free utility — you built your OAuth flow, mapped your data models, and pulled as much data as you needed. That era is over.
The new pricing model hinges on a distinction between two API call classifications:
- <cite index="1-27,1-28">**Core API calls** cover most data-in operations such as creating or updating invoices, bills, customers, vendors, etc. Core API calls are unmetered and uncharged.</cite> Intuit wants to encourage third-party applications to push data into their ecosystem, so writes remain completely free.
- <cite index="1-29">**CorePlus API calls** cover most data-out operations such as reading accounts, querying company information, and fetching reports.</cite> These are metered and subject to monthly caps or overage fees.
The classification is determined by the combination of **endpoint and HTTP method**. <cite index="23-20">Only successful API calls — specifically those returning a 2xx HTTP status code — are counted toward metered usage.</cite> <cite index="23-21">API calls executed within the sandbox environment are not included in the new fee structure.</cite>
Put bluntly: if your integration primarily **reads** data from QuickBooks (syncing invoices to your dashboard, pulling chart of accounts, generating reports), you're now paying for it. If you primarily **write** data (creating invoices, updating customer records), you can stay on the free tier indefinitely.
